About PhD supervision
Supervisors are PhD candidates' main point of contact and provide guidance, constructive feedback, and progress oversight, as well as support in forming professional networks and becoming a part of the academic community.
You can also consult the Center for Doctoral Studies' page on supervision for more information about this topic.
If you want to join CoBeNe as a supervisor, please reach out to vds.cobene(at)univie.ac.at.
Who is eligible?
The following persons are eligible to act as supervisors:
University professors
Habilitated academic staff
Associate professors
Assistant professors
You can find faculty members eligible to supervise or co-supervise you in one of our research areas below.
i
According to the study law of the University of Vienna,
“University professors, habilitated staff members, associated professors as well as assistant professors according to the Collective Bargaining Agreement for University Staff of the University of Vienna are entitled to, and in accordance with their other university responsibilities are also obliged to supervise and assess doctoral theses.
Students are entitled to request the supervision of their doctoral thesis of these university employees. Doctoral candidates have to decide on the topic of their doctoral thesis in agreement with the supervisor.
Supervision by more than one person authorised to supervise is admissible.” (UG, §15(2)).

New podcast: Supervisors' Secrets
Every garden has its keeper. Every doctoral journey has its guide. Behind every finished dissertation is a supervisor who knew when to step in, and when to step back. Supervisors' Secrets is a new podcast by supervisors, for (future) supervisors, offering candid, concise conversations about what works, what fails, and what doctoral supervision can look like in practice. Come on in and enjoy this season's episodes with us: the garden gate is open.
